results.question: How do I schedule a building inspection?
results.answer: To schedule a City of Franklin building inspection: 1. Call the inspection request line at 615-591-5603. 2. Provide your permit number and the inspection type needed, such as framing, insulation, rough-in, or final. 3. Call by 12:00 p.m. for a next-business-day inspection. You may also schedule online through the City’s Online Inspection Portal. Online scheduling has a 5:00 a.m. cutoff for same-day inspections. For portal access or trade-permit scheduling, call 615-794-7012, extension 6, or email cofpermitapp@franklintn.gov. Note: Plumbing, mechanical, and electrical inspections require their own permit numbers.

results.question: I found a lost cat. What do I do?
results.answer: If you found a lost cat: 1. Approach calmly and keep it separate from your pets, especially if it seems sick, injured, or frightened. 2. Provide water, shelter, and a small amount of food. Avoid cow’s milk. 3. Check for a collar or ID tag. Have a veterinarian or animal shelter scan for a microchip. 4. Report the found cat to nearby animal shelters and post a photo in local lost-and-found pet groups. Include where and when you found it. 5. Ask nearby residents and check for “lost cat” notices, but don’t share every identifying detail so the owner can confirm ownership. 6. If the cat is injured, contact a veterinarian or animal welfare organization promptly. 7. Be cautious of scams; ask anyone claiming the cat for identifying details or proof. If you cannot safely hold the cat, contact a local animal shelter or animal control agency for guidance.

results.question: I smell gas outside. What should I do?
results.answer: Leave the area immediately and move upwind, away from the suspected leak. Do not use matches, cigarettes, electrical switches, vehicles, or anything that could create a spark nearby. Warn others to stay away if you can do so safely. Once you are well away from the odor, call 911 and report a possible gas leak. Do not return until emergency personnel say it is safe.

results.question: Power lines are down in the road.
results.answer: Stay away—assume the lines are energized. Do not touch them, drive over them, or approach any vehicle or water near them. If the lines are in the roadway or creating immediate danger, call 911 now. In Franklin city limits, you can also report the road hazard to Franklin Police non-emergency at 615-794-2513. If you’re outside Franklin city limits in Williamson County, call the Sheriff’s Office at 615-790-5550. Report the outage to Middle Tennessee Electric as well. (franklintn.gov)

results.question: How do I dispose of paint?
results.answer: For Franklin and Williamson County residents: Latex paint: If the can is empty or has 1 inch or less, remove the lid and let it dry. If more than 1 inch remains, mix in an equal amount of cat litter and let it dry. Once completely dry, place the can—with the lid removed—in your garbage cart. Do not place liquid latex paint in the trash. Latex paint is not accepted at BOPAE. Oil-based paint: Do not dry it out or put it in the trash. Take partially full or full cans to BOPAE at 417 Century Court, Franklin. Hours: Monday–Thursday, 6:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; first Saturday of each month, 8:00 a.m.–noon. Free for Williamson County residents; commercial waste is not accepted. Questions: Franklin Sanitation and Environmental Services, 615-794-1516.

results.question: How do I transfer my child to another school?
results.answer: In Franklin, the process depends on the school district: Williamson County Schools (WCS): 1. Confirm your new address and school zone using the WCS school-zone information. 2. Contact the new zoned school and ask for the enrollment secretary or registrar. 3. Complete enrollment through Skyward. If your child already attends WCS, use your existing Skyward Family Access account. 4. Provide required documents, including proof of residence and, if transferring from another Tennessee public school, the Tennessee School Immunization Certificate or valid exemption. 5. After the new school confirms enrollment, coordinate withdrawal and records transfer with the current school. Franklin Special District (FSD): 1. Contact FSD Central Office or the new school to verify eligibility and available space. 2. For a move or custody change, contact the school; those transfers may continue during the school year. 3. For a transfer to a school outside your attendance zone, submit an out-of-zone waiver. Approval depends on available capacity, and transportation is the parent’s responsibility. 4. FSD Central Office: 615-794-6624, 205 Eddy Lane, Franklin. Do not withdraw your child until the new school confirms acceptance and provides a start date.

results.question: Where do I register for kindergarten?
results.answer: Register online through your zoned school district: Williamson County Schools: Use the WCS Student Enrollment/Registration page. Current WCS families sign in to Skyward and select “WCS New Student Enrollment.” New families request a Skyward account through WCS’s New Student Online Enrollment instructions. For help, contact your zoned elementary school or WCS at 615-472-4000. Franklin Special District: Use the FSD Enrollment and Registration page. Families with an existing Skyward account select “New Student Online Enrollment”; families without one select “Enroll Now.” You may upload documents or submit them at your zoned school. FSD Central Office: 615-794-6624. For the 2026–27 school year, children must be 5 by August 15, 2026. You’ll generally need a birth certificate, immunization record, physical examination, and proof of residence.

results.question: Is there pre-K in Franklin?
results.answer: Yes. Franklin has public pre-K options for the 2026–2027 school year: Franklin Special District offers free, state-funded Voluntary Pre-K for eligible 4-year-olds, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m., at Franklin, Liberty, Johnson, Moore, and Poplar Grove elementary schools. Children generally must live in the Franklin Special District, and families provide transportation. Apply through FSD’s Early Learning program or call Student Support Services at 615-472-3100. FSD also offers a preschool Positive Peer Model program for some 3- and 4-year-olds, including tuition and sliding-scale options. Williamson County Schools also offers Voluntary Pre-K for eligible 4-year-olds.
